intro.name: Descent into Hades
text: There was a time when Orpheus could make the world fall silent.
Kings laid down their crowns to hear him play. Wild beasts gathered at his feet. Even the trees seemed to bend toward the sound of his lyre.
And among all things he loved, none was dearer to him than Eurydice.
But love, like all mortal things, is fragile.
One day, as Eurydice wandered through the fields, a serpent struck from the grass. Its venom spread swiftly through her veins, and before Orpheus could reach her, she was gone.
The world became silent.
Orpheus could not accept it.
He wandered for days and nights, calling her name. At last, with nothing left but grief, he raised his voice to the heavens.
He begged Zeus, ruler of gods and men, to hear the sorrow of a mortal who had lost everything.
And Zeus heard him.
From the heavens descended Hermes, swift messenger of the gods and guide of the souls of the dead.
He led Orpheus beyond the lands of the living, through valleys where no bird sang and beneath skies where no sun could be seen.
At last, they came to a vast stone gate.
Behind it lay the realm of Hades.
Hermes stopped.
Before them stood Cerberus, the hound of the Underworld, its three heads watching from the darkness. Its growl rolled through the earth like distant thunder.
Orpheus stood before the beast, clutching his lyre.
Hermes looked upon him one final time.
—Beyond this gate, Orpheus, you walk alone.
The gates opened.
Darkness swallowed the light.
And somewhere beyond the river of the dead, Eurydice was waiting.
Orpheus stepped into the Underworld.

verse1.name: Into Darkness
text: The gate closed behind him.
Stone stairs led down into shadow.
Somewhere below, a growl echoed.

verse2.name: The Gallery
text: He passed through halls carved by hands older than memory.
The dead had walked these stones for a thousand years.

verse3.name: Cerberus Waits
text: Ahead, the passage opened into a vast chamber.
Three pairs of eyes gleamed in the dark.
The hound was waiting.

outro.name: Outro
text: The three-headed hound lay still, soothed by the lyre.
Beyond the gate the air grew cold and wet, as if the stone itself were drowning.
Orpheus heard it then: a river, black as forgotten names.
The Styx.
He walked toward the sound of oars.

timeout.name: Time runs out
text: The hourglass empties.
Orpheus feels the Underworld claim what time remains.
Before he can reach Eurydice, darkness closes in.
